description: Jeremiah stops mid-rebuke to ask whether any of the prophets had actually been in God's presence. It is an easier question to dodge now than it has ever been.
excerpt: That's a different kind of false prophet than Jeremiah was dealing with, but the root is the same. Speaking for God without ever standing before God.
verse: "Have any of these prophets been in the Lord's presence to hear what he is really saying? Has even one of them cared enough to listen?"
body_html:
This is Jeremiah pausing in the middle of God's rebuke against false prophets to ask a question of his own.

Have any of them actually spent time with God? Or are they just making stuff up?

The same question applies now. I've done it myself. Spouted off some Christianese-sounding soundbite that lands well, gets a nod, maybe even encourages someone, but never actually came from time with God. It came from things I've heard other people say. It came from what sounded right in the moment. It came from wanting to have something spiritual to contribute.

And now with AI, it's even easier.

You can ask a chatbot for a Bible verse on any topic. You can ask it to write a devotional. You can ask it to draft a prayer, a caption, a comforting text to a hurting friend. What comes back sounds spiritual. It uses the right words. It might even be technically true. But it didn't come from a conversation with God. It came from a computer.

That's a different kind of false prophet than Jeremiah was dealing with, but the root is the same. Speaking for God without ever standing before God.

Jeremiah's question needs to land on all of us. Have I been in the Lord's presence to hear what He's really saying? Or am I just repeating what sounds spiritual?

The tell in Jeremiah's day was that the false prophets always said what people wanted to hear. Peace. Comfort. Don't worry. Nothing bad will happen. Meanwhile the real prophets were calling people to turn, to repent, to actually change. That's still a decent test. If everything I'm saying about God just makes people feel good about wherever they already are, I might not be speaking from God's presence at all.

Time with Him has to come first. Then the words that come out of us have a chance of actually being His.

When was the last time you spoke about God from His presence, and when was the last time you spoke about Him from a script?
question: When was the last time you spoke about God from His presence, and when was the last time you spoke about Him from a script?
